headline: Cloud demand surges, AI buildout compresses margins
summary_short: Oracle's fiscal Q4 2026 revenue rose 21% y/y to $19.2B on 47% cloud growth (Cloud Infrastructure up 93%), with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.45 and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.11; Remaining Performance Obligations jumped to $638B, up $85B sequentially, largely on prepaid AI infrastructure contracts.
summary_long: Cloud revenue (IaaS+SaaS) grew 47% y/y to $9.9B, led by 93% growth in Cloud Infrastructure on AI training/inferencing demand; Cloud Applications grew 10%. Software license revenue kept declining (-2% y/y) as customers migrate on-premise workloads to the cloud. GAAP operating income rose 20% to $6.1B despite an $823M restructuring charge; non-GAAP operating income hit a record $8.6B (+22%). RPO reached $638B, up $85B q/q, mostly large prepaid or customer-supplied-hardware AI contracts. FY2026 operating cash flow rose 54% to $32.0B, but free cash flow was -$23.7B on $55.7B of annual AI-datacenter capex. Oracle guided Q1 FY2027 revenue growth of 27-29% y/y, reaffirmed $90B FY2027 revenue guidance, and raised FY2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $8.05.
